text:
The American Chamber of Commerce in Korea (AMCHAM) hosted a special luncheon on Wednesday with U.S. Ambassador to Korea Michelle Park Steel and Gen. Xavier Brunson, commander of the United Nations Command, Combined Forces Command and U.S. Forces Korea (USFK).
The event in Seoul commemorated the 250th anniversary of the United States and drew about 200 participants, including representatives from AMCHAM member companies and other Korean and international businesses.
Under the theme “The U.S.-ROK Alliance in a Changing World: Strengthening Security, Prosperity & Partnership,” the luncheon explored the alliance’s evolving role and ways to deepen security and economic cooperation.
“It is a tremendous honor to host two of America’s most important leaders in Korea, representing the military and diplomatic pillars of our alliance,” AMCHAM Chairman James Kim said.
“The U.S.-Korea alliance is stronger, broader and more important than ever. Our alliance is built on a strong foundation of security. Today, that partnership extends far beyond defense — connecting our economies, our industries and our people,” he said.
Kim highlighted cooperation in shipbuilding, semiconductors, batteries, aerospace and defense, saying the two countries are developing industries critical to economic and national security.
“Economic security and national security now go hand in hand. And at AMCHAM, we are committed to strengthening both,” he said.
Steel and Brunson delivered special addresses before joining a fireside conversation moderated by Kim.
The discussion covered the changing security environment, Korea’s evolving international role, alliance priorities and the future of USFK. The participants also explored how Korea could leverage its defense and manufacturing capabilities to become a regional sustainment hub, strengthen military readiness and expand defense-industrial cooperation.
On economic security, the conversation focused on policy coordination to support business investment and innovation. Topics included regulatory predictability, a level playing field in the digital sector, U.S. energy investment and cooperation in liquefied natural gas.
Kim reaffirmed AMCHAM’s commitment to turning dialogue into practical outcomes and serving as a bridge between the governments and business communities of the two countries.
The luncheon came as security and economic issues have become increasingly interconnected, underscoring the importance of closer cooperation between Korea and the U.S. across defense, energy and strategic industries.
